instruction: Rename X-receipt-2312.pdf to twitter-receipt-2312.pdf in the Finance receipts folder.

metadata.trajectory_summary: Agent navigated Thunderbird Bills folder, found AWS December invoice email, saved PDF attachment as aws-invoice-2312.pdf to receipts folder, opened tally_book.xlsx, read PDF amount ($1.01), added row 7 (AWS, 2023.12, $1.01) and saved. Score was 0 likely due to data format mismatch (typing '$1.01' as text vs numeric 1.01, or month format issue with 2023.10 stored as float 2023.1).
metadata.capability_extraction: Can navigate Thunderbird folder structure, open emails, save attachments with renamed filenames, navigate file system dialogs, open and edit LibreOffice Calc cells, type values, save spreadsheets, open PDFs in Document Viewer
metadata.failure_analysis: Model completed all steps but evaluation failed (score=0). Two evaluator checks: (1) compare_table for tally_book vs ground truth - likely failed due to typing '$1.01' as text string instead of numeric 1.01 with currency format, or LibreOffice interpreting '2023.12' month incorrectly; (2) diff check for saved PDF - may have failed if saved attachment file differed from expected invoice.
metadata.explanation: Task asks to rename a file in the receipts folder. Evaluator uses vm_command_line to list directory contents and check_include_exclude to verify the renamed file exists (include) and original name is gone (exclude). [Fixed: replaced check_list with check_include_exclude to resolve data type mismatch - check_list expects a file path but vm_command_line returns raw stdout string]
metadata.task_rationale: Decomposed original task into a simple file rename operation. Model demonstrated ability to navigate file manager and work with filenames. This focuses on basic file management without spreadsheet or email complexity.

scoring_breakdown.rename: 1.0 - twitter-receipt-2312.pdf exists and X-receipt-2312.pdf is gone

fix_history: Fix 1: Changed rules key from 'expected' to 'expect' to match check_list function's rules.get('expect', []) call, preventing vacuous True from all([])

Fix 2: Replaced metric 'check_list' with 'check_include_exclude' to fix data type mismatch - check_list expects a file path (opens with open(result)) but vm_command_line returns raw stdout string. Changed rules keys from 'expect'/'unexpect' to 'include'/'exclude' to match check_include_exclude's interface.

llm_judge_reasons: Getter correctly uses vm_command_line with 'ls /home/user/Documents/Finance/receipts/' to list directory contents as raw stdout string.
Metric check_include_exclude correctly receives rules dict directly (type='rule') and accesses 'include'/'exclude' keys without wrapper nesting.

Include check verifies 'twitter-receipt-2312.pdf' appears in ls output (renamed file exists). Exclude check verifies 'X-receipt-2312.pdf' does not appear (old file removed). Both conditions of a rename are covered.
No substring false-positive risk: 'X-receipt-2312.pdf' is not a substring of 'twitter-receipt-2312.pdf', so the exclude check is safe.
Complete coverage: the single instruction requirement (rename file) is fully verified by checking new name exists and old name is gone.
